title: WPMS/249/2015 of Sriram Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPMS No. 249 of 2015
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Mr. Jitendra Chaudhary, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mr. A.K. Joshi, Addl. C.S.C. for the
State.
Present petition is filed assailing the
order dated 29th December, 2014, passed by
the respondent No. 3 whereby permanent
resident certificate issued earlier in favour of
the petitioner was cancelled / revoked.
It is specially mentioned in the
impugned order that vide letter dated
12.09.2013, petitioner was required to show
cause as to why his permanent resident
certificate be not cancelled in view of the
complaint made by Shri Kali Charan; despite
show cause notice dated 12.09.2013,
petitioner did not furnish his reply, therefore,
allegation made in the complaint as well as
in the inquiry report submitted by the Naib
Tehsildar stand unrebutted.
Perusal of annexure No. 21 of the writ
petition reveals that petitioner has submitted
his reply to the show cause notice dated
12.09.2013 which was duly received in the
office of respondent No. 3 on 27.09.2013.
Therefore, observation of respondent No. 3
in the impugned order that no reply was
furnished seems to be incorrect.
Mr. A.K. Joshi, Addl. C.S.C.,
appearing for respondents fairly submitted
that fact remains that petitioner could not be
heard by the respondent No. 3 prior to the

passing of the impugned order, therefore,
respondent No. 3 shall pass fresh appropriate
order in accordance with law after hearing
the petitioner preferably within eight weeks
from today. Petitioner, if so advised, may
also file his supplementary explanation
before the respondent No. 3 annexing
therewith copy of the annexure No. 21 within
one week from today and thereafter
petitioner shall also be heard.
In view of the above, present petition
stands allowed. Impugned order is hereby
quashed. Petitioner may file his
supplementary explanation to the show cause
notice within a week from today annexing
therewith copy of the annexure No. 21
whereupon respondent No. 3 shall hold fresh
inquiry and shall pass appropriate fresh
orders in accordance with law after hearing
the petitioner within next seven weeks.
CLMA No. 1149 of 2015 also stands
disposed of accordingly.
(Alok Singh, J.)
Dated 23.01.2015
Shiv
